gapDispositions.angle: Structured/predictable classical-control context versus dynamic/partially unknown sensor-driven adaptation, without claiming classical control is categorically incapable of such environments.
gapDispositions.reason: The environment contrast is separately tested from hybrid integration, with an explicit limit on the pedagogical comparison. Alternatives reverse the row or confuse feedback/learning and integration/replacement. Easy recall is accurately labeled.

gapDispositions.angle: The source architecture branches Sensor Fusion (EKF) toward both SLAM and AMCL before navigation.
gapDispositions.reason: The actual EKF branch endpoints are SLAM and AMCL. Alternatives distinguish serial and parallel paths and other layers. This is source-schematic reading, not a claim of actual subscriptions.

gapDispositions.angle: Desired wheel velocity → PID → PWM output → DC motor → wheel-encoder feedback, including feedback for continuing correction.
gapDispositions.reason: The source separates desired velocity, PID, PWM, motor plant and encoder measurement, and the text states continuing correction. The question does not invent a drawn feedback-return arrow. Alternatives confuse command/measurement or remove feedback use.

gapDispositions.angle: Identify the separately labeled Global Planned Path and Local Planner Path in the actual screenshot.
gapDispositions.reason: The screenshot annotations distinguish the leftward long global path from the short local path by the robot. Alternatives swap labels or misidentify obstacle and odometry elements; no metric or performance inference is made.

gapDispositions.angle: Processing Nodes has one output branch toward Navigation and another downward to Motor Controller → Mobile Robot.
gapDispositions.reason: The two processing outputs and subsequent controller-to-robot arrow are read directly. Alternatives invert, bypass or serialize arrows absent from the drawing; no scheduling inference is made.
